images.filename: URN NBN no-nb digifoto AE0000029882 0015 F 01 Goebbels in Nazi occupied Norway 1940-11-29 WW2 German cruiser Blücher memorial Askholmene Oslofjorden General Engelbrecht Korvettenkapitän Ruhfus G W Mueller. Ottar Gladtvet Nasjonalbib.jpg
images.caption:
Propaganda Minister Joseph Goebbels attends a memorial service at the Blücher monument, Oscarsborg
 Joseph Goebbels, propaganda minister in Nazi Germany, visits the memorial of the German cruiser «Blücher» during his visit to German occupied Norway from November 28 to December 1, 1940. The monument was a German memorial for German losses when Norwegian artillery at  Oscarsborg fortress sank the warship during the attack on Norway during World War II on April 9, 1940.
The picture was taken on November 29, 1940, in the Drøbak Sound in the Oslofjord and shows, besides Goebbels, among others:
Ministerialrat Georg Wilhelm Müller, Goebbels' former adjutant responsible for press, culture, and information in German-occupied Norway during World War II
Korvettänkaptän Heinrich Ruhfus, Kriegsmarine naval commander in Oslo
General Erwin Engelbrecht. He was the commander of the German infantry forces aboard the Blücher, which was meant to secure the Norwegian capital during the attack on Norway in April 1940. After the ship sank during the battle at Oscarsborg fortress, he managed to avoid drowning by swimming ashore on the Askholmene islets.
The German-controlled Norwegian newspaper Aftenposten featured two photographs marked from the event and the following short text on Saturday, November 30, 1940: (...) Reichsminister Goebbels, during his visit to Oslo, paid a visit to the monument for those who fell from the great cruiser "Blücher" and at the fortress Oscarsborg. He honored the dead from "Blücher" by laying a wreath, after which Lieutenant General Engelbrecht and Oslo's naval commander, Korvettänkaptän Ruhfus, described the course of the battles for Oslo in detail.
The picture is copied from "negatives by filmmaker and director Ottar Gladtvet (assumed)"
